title: VIP Play, Inc. 8-K Filing — 2026-04-20
summary: VIP Play, Inc., a Nevada micro-cap company, disclosed the terms of its First Amended and Restated Discretionary Convertible Revolving Line of Credit Demand Note with Excel Family Partners, LLLP. The note carries a 12% fixed annual interest rate and allows Excel to convert outstanding debt into common stock at 80% of the lowest recent share price within the prior 12 months. As of April 20, 2026, the aggregate outstanding principal balance was $24,500,626 — which exceeds the stated $14,000,000 maximum, an inconsistency not explained in the filing.
key_points: VIP Play, Inc. entered into a convertible revolving credit note with Excel Family Partners, LLLP controlled by a company insider (Bruce Cassidy, Secretary and sole board member)
The note maximum principal amount is $14,000,000 with outstanding balance of $24,500,626 as of April 20, 2026
Interest rate is fixed at 12% per annum; default rate increases to 14% (Fixed Rate + 2%)
Excel has conversion rights to common stock at 80% of the Lowest Recent Price within a 12-month lookback period; if no shares sold in that period, conversion price defaults to $0.50 per share
The company borrowed an additional $1,214,313 across seven draws from February 20, 2026 through April 17, 2026
Note is due and payable upon demand, with no stated maturity date
why_it_matters: This is a routine corporate debt disclosure for a micro-cap company. It does not contain information relevant to macroeconomic policy, market structure, or broader market catalysts. The note terms (related-party transaction, demand feature, above-market interest rate, conversion rights with dilution potential) are material only to VIP Play's shareholders and are typical for thinly capitalized companies. Note: The outstanding balance ($24,500,626) exceeds the stated maximum principal ($14,000,000), suggesting either an uncapped facility or undisclosed additional borrowings.
